chapter: Tatum, Wiggins and Los Angeles friends
title: Tears at Bracknell and the North Sea Jazz Festival with the Newton quintet
summary: Callender describes arranging "Lush Life" and "Chelsea Bridge" for the European trip and being moved by the audience reaction, and why America lacks it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Incidentally, coming back to the European trip with the James Newton Quintet, most of the music was original music except for two things that I arranged for the group. One was "Lush Life" featuring tuba and bassoon, and the other was "Chelsea Bridge" which was a tuba solo. And I'll come back to another point. At Bracknell, outside of London, we closed a concert, and that was...I told you, it brought tears to my eyes, the reception we got. I had never seen

anything like it. And one other place, at Den Haag, or the Northsea Jazz Festival, the same thing happened. The reception was so marvelous until you... Well, I'm not a crybaby, but these kind of reactions do bring tears. And these people were so wonderful to us, I wonder why the same thing doesn't happen in our own country.

I guess because not enough people are exposed to know that you're good here. I mean, the people that know about you are certainly moved. I mean, the audience at Santa Monica was. But there's not enough people who are aware of the music.
Yeah. I don't mean me necessarily; I just mean the whole what they call Jazz.
It's our culture, and they are closer to it...
